consensus_findings: Across lanes, FY2026 preserves Walmart's broad omnichannel, cyber, trade, fintech, and litigation scaffold rather than rewriting it from scratch.
All lanes identify customer-interface risk from AI-enabled search, discovery, recommendation, and emerging agentic platforms as the clearest new business-facing sharpening.
Multiple lanes agree that FY2026 makes cyber risk more concrete by explicitly describing AI-amplified attacks and keeps tariff pressure more immediate into fiscal 2027.
The broad change is better read as a calm operating shift with sharper examples than as a dramatic new thesis.
disagreement_findings: P2 is the clearest first read because it most explicitly separates selective sharpenings from broad structural continuity.
P1 stays useful on the same evidence packet, but it reads a bit more like a broad retail-and-AI update than a carefully bounded operating shift.
P0 catches the broad AI and tariff movement, but it is less disciplined about where refreshed examples should stop carrying novelty claims.
why_this_case_matters: WMT belongs in the public casebook because it proves that a calm case can still be distinctive. The value is not drama; the value is that customer-interface risk, AI-amplified cyber exposure, and tariff persistence sharpen enough to change how the filing should be read.
investor_read: The practical shift is that FY2026 no longer treats AI mainly as an internal efficiency theme. It makes AI-mediated shopping, search, discovery, advertising, and purchasing a more direct customer-interface risk while also sharpening cyber and tariff persistence. The investor question is whether those selective additions now matter more than the reused omnichannel scaffold.
protocol_read: Methodologically, this is a strong calm case because the same tagged packet can support either a disciplined selective-shift answer or a broader novelty claim. P2 best preserves the calm boundary, P1 remains useful but broader, and P0 shows how a simple control can overread refreshed specifics.
caveat: This remains a paragraph-packet case view on the official FY2025 to FY2026 pair. It supports a public judgment about selective sharpening and boundedness, but it does not prove a benchmark result or justify shipping outline compare in this pass.
